replies.q: explain what an anchored vwap band bounce is in one paragraph
replies.reply: An anchored VWAP band bounce occurs when price reaches and rejects the upper or lower standard deviation bands of a Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP) calculation that is tied to a specific historical point, such as a major swing high/low, an earnings date, or a significant news event. Unlike a rolling VWAP, an anchored VWAP represents the average price paid by all participants since that specific "anchor" date. The bands create a volatility envelope around this average; a "bounce" happens when price hits a band and reverses, signaling that the market is either exhausted at a high-volume extreme or finding support/resistance based on the cumulative volume profile of the move since that anchor.

replies.reply: An anchored VWAP band bounce occurs when the price reaches the upper or lower standard deviation bands of a volume-weighted average price (VWAP) calculation that begins at a specific structural anchor, such as an earnings report or a major swing high or low. These bands represent price levels where the market has historically balanced volume and price since that specific starting point. A "bounce" is the price action of the asset rejecting one of these bands and reversing, signaling that the market is treating that level as a significant zone of support or resistance relative to the volume-weighted average of the period.
